content.text: extend arms -push against wall; observe scapula
: visual protrusion of scapula, or winging
Direction of winging localize n.          -  medial: long thoracic n.          -  lateral: trapezius, CN XI
- asymmetry: dislocation, atrophy, or AC separation
- squaring, loss of round contour: dislocation or deltoid atrophy (axillary n.)
- SITS atrophy: chronic cuff tear, suprascapular n.
- arm held added, internally rotated: dislocation, guarding
Localize tender to a specific structure
- humerus greater tuberosity      -   scapula (incl. bony spine)
- Areas of tenderness: AC: AC patho
SITS muscles:          -    synovial membrane beneath A & P acromion
- biceps tendon      -    subacromial subdeltoid bursa   -     rhomboid
Active-only loss w full passive ROM: cuff tear
- painful, weak: supraspinatus                     - global loss: frozen shoulder
add: Apley scratch test -thumb behind back & hold
- loss: adhesive capsulitis                              - pain at end ER: instability
Each plane isolates a specific cuff muscle
Musc atrophy of SUPRA/Infraspinatus muscles: rotator cuff tear
- weak IR: subscapularis                        - weak ER: infraspinatus, teres minor
Impingement: repetitive cuff compression b/n humeral head & acromion
Cycle: rotator cuff rub b/n humerus & top edge of shoulder -> swell & narrow space -> ↑pain, ↑irritation
Painful arc reflects cuff compression under acromion
Compress greater tuberosity against A. acromion
palm face ↓ in front of chest
- 1 hand on forearm & 1 hand on arm
- Compress greater tuberosity against supraspinatus tendon & coracoacromial ligament
- arm to 90’ & IR arms (↓thumb) -> empty can
Abd arm to 90’ (shoulder) -pt slowly lower arm
- Shoulder forward flexed to 90’, 15’ add, forearm pronated, pt resists ↓force
repeat w arms ER while 15’ add & forearm supinated, pt resists ↓force
Pain deep, relieved by supination (worse w IR)
Deep v superficial pain separate labrum from AC
elbow flexed to 90’, forearm in neutral position
- elbow neutral close to thorax, feel biceps groove on shoulder
- pt & examiner move glenohumeral joint simultaneously into ER (proximal radioulnar joint into supination) -ask pt to ⍉move
subluxation or transverse humoral  lig tear
Stand/sit w arm resting at side, closest  to body
- Stabilize shoulder, straighten elbow, supinate hand, & raise arm forward ~90’
